metaTitle: About — Candice P. Chu, DVM, PhD, DACVP
metaDescription: Biography, leadership, education and honors of Candice P. Chu — veterinary clinical pathologist and Assistant Professor at Texas A&M University.
bio: Candice P. Chu, DVM, PhD, DACVP, is a board-certified veterinary clinical pathologist and Assistant Professor in the Department of Veterinary Pathobiology at Texas A&M University. Her work focuses on veterinary artificial intelligence, digital cytology, diagnostic AI, large language models, and AI education.

She earned her DVM from National Taiwan University, then completed a PhD in veterinary pathobiology and a residency in veterinary clinical pathology at Texas A&M University, becoming a Diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Pathologists in 2021. Before returning to Texas A&M in 2024, she served as Assistant Professor of Clinical Pathology at the University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine.

Dr. Chu develops and evaluates AI methods for veterinary diagnostics—from lymphoid cell classification in cytology images to structured data extraction from clinical records—while building curricula that prepare veterinary students and professionals to use AI responsibly. Her molecular work pursues non-invasive microRNA biomarkers for chronic kidney disease in dogs and cats, connecting companion-animal nephrology to human disease through a One Health lens.

She co-chairs the ACVP Pathology Informatics Committee, serves on the AVMA Task Force on Emerging Technologies and Innovation, the Association of American Veterinary Medical Colleges AI Working Group, and the Texas A&M University AI Steering Committee.

contact.title: Contact & Collaboration
contact.body: Dr. Chu welcomes enquiries about research collaboration, speaking invitations, graduate study, and AI curriculum development. Her full record of publications, grants, teaching and service is available on request.

shortBio: Dr. Candice Chu is an Assistant Professor of Clinical Pathology at Texas A&M University, where she develops and validates AI tools for veterinary diagnostics, including deep learning models for cytology and benchmarking of large language models for clinical records. She teaches AI literacy to DVM students, serves on multiple AI task forces and committees, and speaks frequently on AI at veterinary meetings.
